info.title: dotnet-bld
info.description: Tool to clean build output folders for msbuild, dotnet build

commands.name: clean
commands.description: Cleans solution / project build output (bin/obj etc.)

options.name: --markdown
options.description: Emit markdown table output where supported. [default: False]

options.name: --root
options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --depth
options.description: If root is a directory, recursion depth to search for .sln or project files. [default: 3]

options.name: --non-current
options.description: Only clean directories for non-current target frameworks. [default: False]

options.name: --obj
options.description: Also clean BaseIntermediateOutputPath (obj folder). [default: False]

options.name: --keep-assets
options.description: When cleaning obj, preserve NuGet restore artifacts (project.assets.json etc.) and only delete build output subdirectories. [default: False]

options.name: --publish
options.description: Also clean publish output (PublishDir) and pack output (PackageOutputPath), including artifacts/publish and artifacts/package in the artifacts layout. [default: False]

options.name: --test-results
options.description: Also clean TestResults directories (dotnet test output: .trx, coverage) next to each project and its solution. [default: False]

options.name: --interactive
options.description: Pick the directories from a list grouped by project: b/o/p/g/t toggle bin, obj, publish, package and test results for every project on the top line or for one project on its line, space toggles a directory, enter confirms. --obj/--publish/--test-results only decide what starts out checked. With --delete the picker is the confirmation. Needs an interactive terminal. [default: False]

options.name: --log
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]

options.name: --output-file
options.description: Path to the output file. [default: clean.sh]

options.name: --force
options.description: Do not ask for confirmation (requires explicit root). [default: False]

options.name: --vstoolspath
options.description: Explicit value for VSToolsPath. If not specified, the tool tries to resolve VSToolsPath either from environment variable or via vswhere.exe. VSToolsPath contains additional msbuild target files which may be required for evaluation of project files.

options.name: --novstoolspath
options.description: Do not try to resolve VSToolsPath from ENV or vswhere.exe. [default: False]

options.name: --concurrency
options.description: Degree of parallelism for project evaluation. Use 1 for sequential processing. [default: 2]

commands.name: containerize
commands.description: Analyze Dockerfiles and .NET projects with SDK container build properties (PublishProfile=DefaultContainer, ContainerBaseImage, or ContainerImage), or migrate Dockerfiles to those properties.

options.description: Emit markdown table output where supported. [default: False]

options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --log
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]

options.name: --list
options.description: Only list Dockerfiles without parsing details. [default: False]

options.name: --projects
options.description: Scan for .NET projects with container build properties. [default: False]

options.name: --all
options.description: Scan for both Dockerfiles and .NET container projects. [default: False]

options.name: --migrate
options.description: Migrate each Dockerfile to SDK container properties (ContainerBaseImage, ContainerPort, ContainerEnvironmentVariable, ...) on the project it builds. Dry run unless --apply is given. [default: False]

options.name: --apply
options.description: With --migrate, write the properties into the project files (default is dry-run). [default: False]

options.name: --delete-dockerfile
options.description: With --migrate --apply, delete the migrated Dockerfile and remove the Visual Studio container-tools settings (Docker* properties, Microsoft.VisualStudio.Azure.Containers.Tools.Targets) from the project. [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description: With --migrate, migrate a Dockerfile even when its runtime stage has instructions the SDK cannot express (RUN, VOLUME, HEALTHCHECK, files copied from the build context). They are listed and dropped. [default: False]

commands.name: outdated
commands.description: Check for outdated NuGet packages and optionally update them to latest versions.

options.name: --markdown
options.description: Emit markdown table output where supported. [default: False]

options.name: --root
options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --depth
options.description: If root is a directory, recursion depth to search for .sln or project files. [default: 3]

options.name: --apply
options.description: Apply package updates instead of just checking. [default: False]

options.name: --skip-tfm-check
options.description: Skip target framework compatibility checking when suggesting package updates. [default: False]

options.name: --prerelease
options.description: Include prerelease versions of NuGet packages. [default: False]

options.name: --orphaned
options.description: List PackageVersion entries in Directory.Packages.props with no matching PackageReference and a newer version on NuGet. Works for both project and solution input. Report-only. [default: False]

options.name: --comment-orphans
options.description: On --apply, comment out outdated orphan PackageVersion entries in Directory.Packages.props. Only honored when the input is a solution (.sln / .slnx / .slnf), since a single project cannot see all consumers of the CPM file. Implies --orphaned for reporting. [default: False]

options.name: --interactive
options.description: Pick the packages to update from a grouped list before applying, and the target version per package (space toggles, left/right change the target, enter confirms, esc cancels). Dependency conflicts between what you picked and what stays are surfaced so you can include the other package, skip the picked one, or accept the risk. Implies --apply and needs an interactive terminal. [default: False]

options.name: --max-bump
options.description: Largest version step to propose, relative to the version a package is pinned at now: 'major' (no cap), 'minor' (same major, no breaking change per SemVer) or 'patch' (same major and minor). Versions above the cap are reported in the 'held' column instead of being applied. [default: Major]

options.name: --max-bump-for
options.description: Override --max-bump for the packages matching a pattern: "<pattern>=<major|minor|patch>". Same wildcard syntax as --package, may be repeated, accepts ';'-separated lists. The most specific matching pattern wins.

options.name: --group-by
options.description: How --interactive groups the packages it offers: 'prefix' (common package id prefix, the default), 'bump' (patch/minor/major) or 'none' (one flat list). When given explicitly, the report table is grouped the same way. [default: Prefix]

options.name: --group-depth
options.description: Maximum prefix length in dot-separated segments for --group-by prefix. [default: 2]

options.name: --group-min
options.description: Smallest number of packages a --group-by prefix group must have; smaller ones are dissolved into '(other)'. [default: 2]

options.name: --preselect
options.description: Which packages --interactive starts out with a check mark on: 'all' (the default), 'no-major', 'patch' or 'none'. [default: All]

options.name: --package
options.description: Only consider packages whose id matches one of these patterns. Supports '*' wildcards, is case-insensitive, may be repeated, and accepts ';'-separated lists. Default: all packages.

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Skip packages whose id matches one of these patterns. Same syntax as --package and applied after it.

options.name: --allow-conflicts
options.description: Update packages even when a dependency they require stays at a version that does not satisfy their declared range. Without this, such packages are held back. [default: False]

options.name: --verify-restore
options.description: After --apply, run 'dotnet restore' on the input and fail the command if NuGet reports errors. The only check that sees what NuGet actually resolves. [default: False]

options.name: --source
options.description: Package source(s) to query: the name of a source in nuget.config or a v3 feed URL. May be repeated. Overrides nuget.config, including package source mapping. Default: the enabled sources from the nuget.config hierarchy, or nuget.org if there is none.

options.name: --ignore-source-mapping
options.description: Query every enabled source for every package instead of honoring the packageSourceMapping section of nuget.config. [default: False]

options.name: --ignore-policy
options.description: Do not apply the package policy rules saved under BLD_HOME (policy.json) for this run. --max-bump-for still applies. [default: False]

options.name: --eval-cache
options.description: Skip the MSBuild evaluation of a project configuration when every file that fed its last evaluation is unchanged (kept under BLD_HOME or the local application data folder). Opt-in: MSBuild properties set through environment variables are not detected. [default: False]

options.name: --log
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]

options.name: --vstoolspath
options.description: Explicit value for VSToolsPath. If not specified, the tool tries to resolve VSToolsPath either from environment variable or via vswhere.exe. VSToolsPath contains additional msbuild target files which may be required for evaluation of project files.

options.description: Do not try to resolve VSToolsPath from ENV or vswhere.exe. [default: False]

options.name: --concurrency
options.description: Degree of parallelism for project evaluation. Use 1 for sequential processing. [default: 2]

commands.name: undo
commands.description: Revert the package updates a previous 'outdated --apply' run wrote to this input. Only values that still read as that run left them are touched; the rest is reported and left alone.

options.name: --markdown
options.description: Emit markdown table output where supported. [default: False]

options.name: --root
options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --list
options.description: List the recorded runs for this input, newest first, and exit. [default: False]

options.name: --run
options.description: Which recorded run to revert: 1 is the newest (the default), 2 the one before, as numbered by --list. [default: 1]

options.name: --package
options.description: Only revert packages whose id matches one of these patterns. Same syntax as outdated --package.

options.name: --exclude
options.description: Leave packages whose id matches one of these patterns as they are. Applied after --package.

options.name: --interactive
options.description: Pick the packages to revert from a grouped list (space toggles, a/n all or none, enter reverts, esc cancels). Needs an interactive terminal. [default: False]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Revert without asking. Required when there is no interactive terminal. [default: False]

options.name: --verify-restore
options.description: After reverting, run 'dotnet restore' on the input and fail the command if NuGet reports errors. [default: False]

options.name: --log
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]

options.name: --markdown
options.description: Emit markdown table output where supported. [default: False]

options.name: --root
options.description: Root directory, .sln, or project file. Can also be specified as trailing argument.

options.name: --depth
options.description: If root is a directory, recursion depth to search for .sln or project files. [default: 3]

options.name: --from
options.description: Source target framework(s) (e.g., net8.0 or net8.0,net9.0 for multiple). If not specified, will be auto-detected from project files.

options.name: --to
options.description: Target framework to migrate to (e.g., net9.0).

options.name: --apply
options.description: Apply changes (default is dry-run). [default: False]

options.name: --update-packages
options.description: With --apply, run `outdated --apply` on the same input after the migration, so packages are updated to versions that support the new target framework, within --max-bump and the saved package policies. As in outdated, only the Release configuration is evaluated and references under a Condition are left alone. [default: False]

options.name: --max-bump
options.description: With --update-packages: largest version step to propose, as in `outdated --max-bump`. [default: Major]

options.name: --update-global-json
options.description: With --apply, set sdk.version in the governing global.json to the highest installed SDK of the target framework's major when the current pin cannot build it. Without --apply, report what would change. [default: False]

options.name: --log
options.description: Log verbosity (Debug, Verbose, Info, Warning, Error). [default: Warning]
